content.text: I couldn't see the source, so this diagnosis comes from the symbol names and the usual structure of this NestJS boilerplate. It is a best guess, not confirmed against the code.

candidates.explanation: This is the most likely cause, and I'm inferring it from the usual shape of this boilerplate rather than from the code itself. The method resolves the photo from the payload and then passes it to the repository together with the rest of the payload. A first-name-only edit has no `photo` field. If the photo variable defaults to `null` instead of `undefined`, or the payload is spread with an explicit `photo` key, the repository gets `photo: null` and clears the avatar. A partial update must leave `photo` undefined unless the client sends `photo` explicitly: an id to set it, or `null` to remove it.

This method merges the payload into the existing user through `UserMapper.toDomain` and `toPersistence`, then saves it. If the payload carries `photo: null` or `undefined` keys, or the merge doesn't skip undefined values, it overwrites the stored photo relation. The document repository's `update` (L97) has the same risk.

This is the profile-edit path (PATCH /auth/me). It forwards `AuthUpdateDto` to `usersService.update`. If it builds a new object with an explicit `photo` value, or the DTO transform turns a missing `photo` into `null`, the avatar is cleared whenever only another field such as `firstName` is edited.

fix.description: In UsersService.update, initialise `photo` as `undefined`. Only set it when `clonedPayload.photo?.id` resolves to a file, or set it to `null` when `clonedPayload.photo === null` is passed explicitly. Don't include a `photo` key in the object passed to the repository when it is undefined. Make sure the repository update and mapper `toPersistence` skip undefined fields so an absent photo never overwrites the stored one.
